correctness.rationale: The Fuss–Catalan expression is integral (subtract p times the adjacent lower binomial coefficient from the numerator binomial); its denominator is a p-unit. Kummer gives no carries in n+pn exactly when neighboring digits sum to at most p−1, including n=0 and the padded top digit. There are exactly the indicated adjacency paths for each r≥1. Summing cosines through p−1−i gives sin((p−i)θ_j)/(2 sin(θ_j/2)), and (p+1/2)θ_j=(j+1/2)π gives the signed eigenvalue and eigenvector equation. The distinct absolute eigenvalues and squared projections of the all-ones vector yield the cotangent-squared coefficients; the prime 2 and r=1 require no exception. The positive top eigenvalue lies strictly between 1 and p by primitivity and the nonconstant row sums. The leading term bounds all real density cutoffs between consecutive powers of p. Truncation followed by zero digits proves the characterized closure. Its cylinder covers give the upper dimension and the Perron transition a_ij v_j/(ρ_p v_i) telescopes to measure proportional to ρ_p^(−r+1) times the last-state weight, giving the lower bound. Expanding sine gives the claimed large-p error term. The frozen code and its recorded small-case data were read, not executed; the proof, not those finite checks, establishes C.

evidence: Flip odd-position digits to p−1−d_i to obtain weak alternation with even positions valleys. Then add 1 to the odd-position values only. For r≥2 this is a bijection to strict up-down words over {0,…,p}: every valley is ≤p−1 and every peak ≥1. At r=1 the alphabet count is higher by one.
Fried, Theorem 1, (1), counts strict up-down words over k letters of length n by 1_{n=1}+4/(2k−1) times the absolute sum of sin²(2iπ/(2k−1))/(2cos(2iπ/(2k−1)))^(n+1).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Set k=p+1, n=r and D=2p+1. For i=1,…,p, m_i=D−4i has |m_i|=2j+1 covering each j exactly once and sign (−1)^(p+j). Then cos(2iπ/D)=sin(m_iπ/(2D)) and sin²(2iπ/D)=cos²(m_iπ/(2D)). The factor 4 changes the power r+1 into the audited r−1 with a cot² coefficient; the only common sign is (−1)^(p(r+1)), removed by the absolute value since the audited sum is positive. This is exact term-level coverage, not just an analogous formula.
